content:
emma-cs: FYI — Zephyr onboarding hit intermittent 429s during SDK warmup after a feature flag flip. They repro'd this pattern in staging and prod intermittently.
raj-eng: can you paste the client version and the exact request they used? also — hosted or dedicated?
emma-cs: hosted. client is node-sdk v0.9.3. sample curl they used:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-xxxx" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"hi"}'
```
They ramped from ~10->200 rps over ~30s. First saw auth 401s then a bunch of 429s. Their agent logs (sanitized):
```
[2026-02-24T18:02:12Z] WARN handshake failed: 401 token expired
[2026-02-24T18:02:13Z] INFO token refresh ok
[2026-02-24T18:02:15Z] ERROR request failed: 429 Too Many Requests
[2026-02-24T18:02:16Z] ERROR request failed: 429 Too Many Requests
```
raj-eng: sounds like token churn + burst behavior. Which billing plan are they on? hosted free/standard limits differ. Any proxy in front of their fleet?
marta-ops: they mentioned an internal proxy that multiplexes upstream connections. that could create a bursty pattern where many logical requests collapse onto few TCP connections and then our burst protection trips. alex, any known issue with node-sdk v0.9.3 around token refresh/backoff?
alex-devex: yes — known issue in 0.9.3: simultaneous worker processes can all attempt refresh when TTL<60s, and the backoff was non-jittered causing thundering refreshes. we shipped a fix in v0.9.5: jittered exponential backoff + a small token prefetch when TTL<60s. recommend upgrading. also suggest tuning connection pooling. example config:
```
const client = new Redwood({
  keepAlive: true,
  maxSockets: 50,
  retry: { retries: 4, factor: 2, jitter: true }
});
```
emma-cs: I sent upgrade guidance to Zephyr and asked them to retry with v0.9.5 and set retry.retries=4. I also asked them to add an X-Request-ID header for tracing.
raj-eng: if the upgrade doesn't remove the 429s, we'll check server-side ratebackoff logs and per-account quotas. marta — can you pull rate-limiter logs for acct zephyr-42 for 18:00-18:10 UTC?
marta-ops: on it. quick look: there's a clear spike and most 429s are flagged as "burst_protection" rather than "quota_exceeded". digging into logs suggests many short-lived tokens and replays. if their proxy reuses TCP while rotating auth headers, our prefix caching could be bypassed.
emma-cs: customer replied — after upgrading and adjusting retries, initial tests were stable for ~2m, then one 429 at 18:06. They attached a header dump showing Authorization rotated roughly every 45s — looks like multiple refreshers active.
alex-devex: that matches the SDK bug. short-term workaround: set REDWOOD_TOKEN_TTL_BUFFER=120 to force refresh earlier (serialized), or add a shared token cache between worker processes. we'll prepare a snippet for them to drop into their init script.
emma-cs: I'll send the workaround and propose a follow-up 30min pairing call to monitor. thanks all :pray:
ingest-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-2213 linked to this thread.
raj-eng: if they still see instability after the workaround, we can schedule a dedicated support session and consider temporary account-level smoothing (whitelist/raise burst threshold) while they patch.
emma-cs: noted. i'll close the loop after 24h stable confirmation.
